relevance_note: The paper reports four patients from two Japanese families with HA20 due to a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant or a 236 kb deletion; 'Four HA20 patients in the two families presented with childhood-onset recurrent oral and genital ulcers and were initially diagnosed and treated as BD'.
method_note: Read the paper, the schema (ha20_v5) and the rules; no other sources. Table 1 gives the four patients as columns, so its cells were read from the row label through that patient's cell; Table 1's columns are, left to right, Patient 1, Patient 2, Patient 3, Patient 4. Symbols: Table 1's legend defines only abbreviations, so per (v3) the '–' cells were NOT used as evidence of absence (those checklist items are 'not reported'); the '+' cells were read as present. Contradiction: Table 1 prints '| Fever | + | + | + | – |' but the text for Patient 4 says 'She presented fever with tonsillitis and lymphadenitis several times a year since her childhood'; I therefore kept the observed phenotypic row from the text, did not emit an excluded row (undefined symbol), and set the checklist item 'recurrent fever' to 'not reported'. No stacked (' / ') cells occurred in any table, so D-31 did not apply. Table 1's 'Musculoskeletal signs –' cells were not read as absence; Patient 4's musculoskeletal absence comes from her own sentence. Excluded from rows: the 5 DECIPHER patients and the 4 healthy DGV/ExAC individuals with TNFAIP3 deletions (counts only, no individual-level detail), the 50 previously reported HA20 cases aggregated in Table 2 (counts only), the 520 BD / 514 Japanese BD / 156 PEDBD comparison cohorts, and the epilepsy control patient. publications.n_patients_reported = 54 because the authors state 'the clinical features of 54 cases with TNFAIP3 variants (50 previously reported cases [5–15] and the four cases described here)'; only the four are described individually. cohort_size_as_stated = 25 (the study's own collected patients). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false: the four patients are described as novel/current. The person mentioned only in the Discussion as having 'a 13 Mb deletion involving TNFAIP3' [8] was included because the paper gives features for him/her. 'amyotrophic lateral sclerosis' (father II-5) was recorded as a phenotypic feature but not mapped to the checklist item 'central nervous system involvement'. 'growth delay' of ref [8] patient was mapped to the checklist item 'growth failure'. Pathogenicity/ACMG were recorded for the family 1 nonsense variant because the paper says 'this variant is classified as pathogenic'; the family 2 deletion is called a 'pathogenic change' only at family level, so its pathogenicity is left 'not reported'. Zygosity is left 'not reported' for all, because the Introduction's 'a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant' is a general statement about the paper's variant, not tied to a named person (D-29). Normal/negative findings (D-27) were recorded as the abnormality they rule out: 'abnormality on colonoscopy' for the two colonoscopy sentences, 'signs of malignant lymphoma' for the biopsy sentence, and 'BD-like symptoms' for the mother and the four maternal relatives; 'neurodevelopmental delay' and 'ophthalmological/neurological/musculoskeletal symptoms' were kept close to the paper's own wording because they name whole examinations rather than single features, so they were mapped to checklist items only where the wording names the item (eye, CNS, musculoskeletal). The aunt 'II-2' is labelled 'II-2 (Family 1)' and the elder brother 'III-1 (Family 1)' because the same pedigree labels are used in the two families.
